output.title: The hidden upkeep in model changes
output.body:
If you are comparing automation with another hire, the quiet cost is not the first build. It is what happens when the model underneath a workflow changes, gets retired, or becomes too awkward to keep using.

For a small business, that can show up in ordinary work like customer-inquiry triage, lead qualification, or invoice handling. A workflow may look fine on day one and still need attention later if the underlying model changes or pricing shifts. That is not a disaster. It is a maintenance decision, and it belongs in the business case from the start.

The practical next step is simple: before you approve an automation pilot, ask one blunt question. If the underlying model is upgraded, retired, or repriced, does the workflow keep working, or do we need to rebuild and pay again? If that is unclear, the plan is not finished yet.

If you are scoping a pilot, make the ongoing model-version decision explicit and keep human approval in place before any re-investment. Automation is only the cheaper option when the workflow is stable and the upkeep is understood.
